questions.title: Gravitational field & potential of the Earth

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: Gravitational field is the force per unit mass acting on a small test mass placed at the point.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.answer: The field lines are radial, pointing towards the centre of the planet.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.answer: For small changes in height, the change in height is very much smaller than the radius of the planet, so (R + h)² ≈ R² — the field lines are approximately parallel and g is approximately constant.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.answer:
At the surface g = GM/R², so 9.81 = 3.99 × 10¹⁴/R²
R = √(3.99 × 10¹⁴/9.81) = 6.38 × 10⁶ m

parts.label: (d)
parts.answer: The potential energy is zero at infinite separation, and the gravitational force is attractive — work is done by the field as the masses come together, so the potential energy falls below zero and is always negative.

questions.title: Thermal equilibrium — ice melting in water

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: The two objects are at the same temperature, so there is no net transfer of thermal energy between them.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.answer: E₁ = XL (the energy to melt the ice at 0 °C).

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.answer: E₂ = Mc(t − θ) (the energy lost by the water cooling from t to θ).

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.answer: E₃ = Xcθ (the energy gained by the melted ice warming from 0 °C to θ).

parts.label: (c)
parts.answer:
Energy is conserved: E₂ = E₁ + E₃, so Mc(t − θ) = XL + Xcθ.
Mct − Mcθ = XL + Xcθ
Mct − XL = θ(Mc + Xc) = θc(M + X)
θ = (Mct − XL)/c(M + X)

questions.title: Ideal gas — r.m.s. speed, temperature & internal energy

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: A gas that obeys pV ∝ T at all values of p, V and T, where T is the thermodynamic temperature.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.answer:
pV = ⅓Nm⟨c²⟩ and Nm/V = ρ, so p = ⅓ρ⟨c²⟩.
1.6 × 10⁵ = ⅓ × 1.9 × ⟨c²⟩
cr.m.s. = √(3 × 1.6 × 10⁵/1.9) = 500 m s⁻¹

parts.label: (c)
parts.answer:
For an ideal gas the molecular potential energy is zero, so the internal energy is the total kinetic energy: U = N × (3/2)kT.
U = 6.0 × 6.02 × 10²³ × (3/2) × 1.38 × 10⁻²³ × 290
= 21000 J

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: Motion in which the acceleration is (directly) proportional to the displacement and is always directed towards a fixed point (in the opposite direction to the displacement).

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.answer: The sphere passes through the equilibrium position in the same direction at t₁ and t₅ (or t₃ and t₇).

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.answer:
The interval t₁ → t₆ is 1.25 periods, so T = 2.2/1.25 = 1.76 s.
f = 1/T = 1.25/2.2 = 0.57 Hz

parts.label: (c)
parts.answer:
v₀ = ωx₀ with ω = 2πf, so x₀ = v₀/(2πf) = 0.080/(2π × 0.57)
= 0.022 m

questions.title: Charged sphere — electric potential, field & capacitance

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: The work done per unit positive charge in moving a small test charge from infinity to the point.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.answer:
E ∝ 1/r², so at the surface (radius r) compared with 3r:
E = 3² × 2.0 × 10⁵ = 1.8 × 10⁶ N C⁻¹

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.answer:
V = Q/4πε₀r and E = Q/4πε₀r², so E = V/r.
r = V/E = 9.0 × 10⁴/1.8 × 10⁶ = 0.050 m = 5.0 cm

questions.title: Coil in a magnetic field — force & torque

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.answer:
torque = force × perpendicular distance between the forces on QR and PS
= 0.064 × 0.025 cos θ = 1.6 × 10⁻³ cos θ N m

parts.label: (a)(iii)
parts.answer: One complete cycle of a sinusoidal curve between 0° and 360°, with the τ axis labelled to show maximum and minimum torque at ±1.6 × 10⁻³ N m: maximum at 0° and 360°, minimum at 180°, and torque zero at 90° and 270°.

parts.label: (b)
parts.answer: The ferrous core increases the magnetic flux density, so the amplitude of the torque increases.

questions.title: Damped oscillations — magnet in a coil & electromagnetic induction

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.answer: Damping is the loss of energy from the oscillations due to resistive forces.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.answer: The amplitude of the oscillations decreases gradually (the oscillations continue for several periods).

parts.label: (a)(iii)
parts.answer: The oscillating magnet cuts magnetic flux, inducing an e.m.f. in the coil. This drives a current through the resistor, which dissipates thermal energy. By conservation of energy this thermal energy comes from the energy of the oscillations, so the oscillations are damped.

parts.label: (b)
parts.answer: For a given induced e.m.f. the current is smaller, so thermal energy is dissipated at a lower rate (the resistive force is smaller). The oscillations are therefore less damped — the amplitude decreases more slowly and they continue for longer.

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: Four diodes (one in each gap of the bridge), each with the correct circuit symbol, all connected in the correct direction (pointing left to right) so that A is at a positive potential with respect to B.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.answer: Three lines showing exponential decay from the peaks at 0.5T, 1.0T and 1.5T, ending where the decay meets the next rising peak, with rising portions following the dotted peaks, and a minimum V of (2/3)V₀.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.answer:
From the graph the discharge time (from V₀ to (2/3)V₀) is (11/30)T.
(2/3)V₀ = V₀ e^(−(11/30)T/τ)
ln(2/3) = −11T/30τ
τ = 0.90 T

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.answer: The time constant increases (τ = RC increases with R), so the capacitor discharges more slowly: the minimum voltage is larger (a smaller difference between the maximum and minimum voltages).

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.answer: Wave–particle duality: an electromagnetic wave can behave like a particle, and a moving particle can behave like a wave.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.answer: λ = h/p, where h is the Planck constant and p is the momentum of the particle.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.answer: The pattern is similar to the diffraction of light, and diffraction is characteristic of wave behaviour — the rings show constructive and destructive interference. This is evidence of a wave nature for the electrons.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.answer: The de Broglie wavelength decreases (λ = h/p and p increases), so the rings become closer together.

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: An alternating p.d. is applied across the crystal, causing it to vibrate. When the frequency of the applied p.d. equals the natural frequency of the crystal it resonates, and this natural frequency is in the ultrasound range — so ultrasound waves are generated.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.answer: Specific acoustic impedance is the product of the density of the medium and the speed of (ultra)sound in the medium (Z = ρc).

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.answer: The reflected fraction α is close to 0 when Z₁ and Z₂ are equal, and close to 1 when Z₁ and Z₂ are very different.

parts.label: (c)
parts.answer:

questions.title: Nuclear fusion in a star — energy, luminosity & temperature

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.answer: Nuclear fusion.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.answer:
Δm = 0.030377 − (3 × 0.002388) = 0.023213 u (the mass difference between the helium-4 and the three deuterium nuclei).
E = Δm c² = 0.023213 × 1.66 × 10⁻²⁷ × (3.00 × 10⁸)²
= 3.47 × 10⁻¹² J

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.answer:
Mass of 1 mol of helium-4 = 4 × 10⁻³ kg. Number of helium-4 nuclei produced per second
= (6.02 × 10²³ × 7.34 × 10¹¹)/(4 × 10⁻³) = 1.10 × 10³⁸ s⁻¹.
Luminosity = (number per second) × (energy per nucleus) = 1.10 × 10³⁸ × 3.47 × 10⁻¹²
= 3.83 × 10²⁶ W
